item.title: Desktop Launcher Creator: giving a launcher to the apps that ship without one
item.description:
Desktop Launcher Creator

Modern Linux desktops receive applications from at least three different worlds: Debian packages, Snap and Flatpak. Each has its own idea of where the application lives and, sometimes, whether it deserves an entry in the applications menu. The result is a familiar annoyance: a program you have installed is there, but you cannot find it — and there is no obvious way to create a launcher for it.

Desktop Launcher Creator is a small GTK application that fixes exactly that. It scans the applications installed through Debian, Snap and Flatpak, shows them in a simple list, and creates a .desktop launcher for whatever you select.

What it does

  • Reads installed applications from the Debian, Snap and Flatpak sources.
  • Shows them in a single list, so you can see what is actually installed.
  • Creates a .desktop launcher for the one you pick, ready to appear in your applications menu.

The interface is intentionally minimal: a source selector (Debian | Snap | Flatpak), the list of applications, a destination and a single action button. No configuration files to hand-edit, no guessing at Exec= lines.

How it is built

The application is written in Python 3.12 with GTK 3 (PyGObject and pycairo). It follows the same philosophy I keep coming back to: keep the core logic independent from the interface, and let the interface be an adapter. In this case the core is “enumerate installed applications and produce a launcher file”; the GTK window is just one way to drive it.

It is licensed under the GPL-3.0-or-later.

Getting it

Pre-built packages are attached to every release:

  • Debian/Ubuntu: .deb
  • Flatpak: .flatpak bundle
  • Snap: .snap
  • AppImage: portable .AppImage
  • Python: wheel and source distribution (.whl, .tar.gz)

You can find them under the Releases section of the project:

  • GitHub: https://github.com/javi-jimenez/desktop-launcher-creator/releases
  • Gitea (self-hosted): https://gitea.app.brisecom.net/gitea/desktop-launcher-creator/releases

Every release is built automatically from a tagged commit, so the artifacts and the source always match.
